title: Photo Print Came Out the Wrong Size? Measure a Proof
description: If a photo prints at the wrong physical size, print a proof at 100% and measure its reference ruler before changing DPI again.
direct: Print a test copy at 100% and measure its 100 mm reference. If the ruler prints at the wrong length, fix scaling before checking the photo size.
figureAlt: A metal ruler checks a printed reference line on a photo proof.
figureCaption: AI-generated conceptual illustration, not an App screenshot, measured result or real export. This image is not an accurate printable ruler; measure the proof from your own file.
cards.choice.heading: File size and paper size differ
cards.choice.body: Pixels and DPI define a nominal image size. The viewer or printer can still fit, shrink or expand that image. Confirm the intended paper size, image dimensions and orientation, then examine the controls in the actual print workflow.
sections.explain.heading: Use the proof as a check
sections.explain.body: A selectable 1:1 detail helps examine a small region, but the screen illustration is not a calibration tool. Printer feed and driver behavior can still affect physical output. Keep the proof settings with the final job so the verified workflow is reproducible.
sections.practice.heading: Share file evidence too
sections.practice.body: It can package exported files with a verification report in a ZIP. Advanced print fitting and batch tools include three successful free advanced exports; basic single-photo DPI changes remain free. Upsampling does not add real detail. The generated photograph depicts measuring a proof and must not itself be printed as an accurate ruler. Check the real proof produced from your own file.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: What if the 100 mm ruler measures 96 mm?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: The output is about 96% of the intended scale. Check the driver for fit-to-page or other scaling and print a fresh proof.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: The ruler measures 100 mm but an edge is missing. What should I check?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Look for cropping and borderless expansion. Measure the intended image area separately from the ruler.

steps.step-1.text: Prepare the intended print size in DPI: Photo Print Prep and review the export’s pixels, both DPI axes and physical dimensions.
steps.step-2.text: Create the app’s 4 × 6 inch PDF proof with its 100 mm ruler. Print at 100% or Actual Size rather than Fit.
steps.step-3.text: Measure the printed ruler with a physical ruler. If it is wrong, check paper-size and scaling settings before judging the photo crop.
